question: GnRH agonist therapy (e.g., monthly depot leuprorelin) is the first-line treatment for peripheral precocious puberty caused by an oestrogen-secreting ovarian cyst.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. GnRH agonists work by down-regulating the HPO axis — they are effective for CENTRAL (GnRH-dependent) precocious puberty. Peripheral PP is driven by a non-HPO source; GnRH agonists do not address this. Treatment targets the cause directly.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — GnRH agonists are NOT appropriate for peripheral precocious puberty. Since peripheral PP is GnRH-independent (the HPO axis is not the source), suppressing GnRH has no effect. Treatment is directed at the peripheral source (e.g., cyst aspiration/resection, aromatase inhibitor).
